findings.title: Private-display paths write source mnemonics to redirected stdout
findings.reproduction: Attach stdin/stderr to a pseudo-terminal but redirect stdout. Call the actual PrivateScreen::enter_to_show and print_phrase functions with the public 128-bit zero-entropy BIP39 fixture, as terminal_display_probe.py does. Trace its three interactive callers.
findings.expected: A private-screen-only reveal must refuse or explicitly obtain consent for a persistent export when the private screen cannot be opened.
findings.observed: The private screen reports inactive, then the callers unconditionally print the source phrase to stdout. The retained probe captured the public mnemonic in the pipe.
findings.impact: Interactive new/wallets/rekey flows can persist an unencrypted phrase in redirected output that the owner intended to contain only encrypted results. The probe uses the shared production display path; it does not replay full Argon2 operations.
findings.recommendedFix: Require a suitable private output terminal before these reveals, or implement a separate explicit export choice that names the destination. Do not silently fall back to ordinary stdout.
findings.requiredVerification: Run PTY regressions for redirected stdout, TERM=dumb, normal terminal, and intentional export. Confirm no phrase is emitted before export consent.

findings.title: Dropping one page-lock guard unlocks another live secret on the same page
findings.reproduction: Run memory_lock_probe.py on Linux. Its final probe uses two distinct live Password allocations sharing a kernel page, then drops one and examines /proc/self/smaps.
findings.expected: A successfully acquired guard must not revoke the memory protection of another live guarded secret.
findings.observed: The synthetic probe records distinct_Password_allocations_share_page=true, live_password_page_locked_after_other_password_drop=false, while the remaining guard still reports locked. Linux mlock locks are page-based and do not stack.
findings.impact: The promised best-effort protection against swapping silently disappears despite successful locking. Actual swap disclosure or secret recovery was not demonstrated; Windows/browser locking remains intentionally unsupported.
findings.recommendedFix: Use page-granular reference counting across guards, or allocations whose locked pages cannot overlap. Make is_locked represent the currently maintained guarantee.
findings.requiredVerification: Exercise overlapping and disjoint allocations, arbitrary drop order, denied mlock, allocation lifetime, and concurrency. Confirm live pages remain locked until the last owning guard drops.

findings.title: The raw terminal input lock ends before its returned secret buffer dies
evidence: Source lifetime inspection at the reviewed commit; independent of AUD-007-SEC002.
findings.reproduction: Trace edit_line: the local LockedPages guard covers its Vec; mem::take moves the allocation into the returned Zeroizing<String>; the guard then drops at function return. Inspect callers retaining or copying that returned string.
findings.expected: A returned secret should retain its acquired page-lock guard for its full owned lifetime, or the limitation must be accurately stated.
findings.observed: The bytes remain owned by the returned String, but the only guard is local to edit_line and unlocks those same pages on return. The raw first password remains alive while a repeat is requested; a new-wallet passphrase is relocked only after the repeat prompt finishes.
findings.impact: Typed secret material can become pageable after input and before its eventual wipe, independent of the overlapping-page defect. No actual swap disclosure was demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Return an owning locked-secret type carrying both bytes and guard, or transfer an equivalent guard to the caller without an unlocked lifetime gap.
findings.requiredVerification: Trace and test the page-lock state after read_line returns and until the returned secret is dropped, including error paths and conversions.

findings.title: Owned private-scalar temporaries are not explicitly zeroized
evidence: Source and type-lifetime inspection at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: Trace key.scalar() in taproot_output_key and the temporary parent scalar in ExtendedKey::child. The scalar type is Copy and has no zeroizing Drop; selected other scalar bindings are explicitly wiped.
findings.expected: The documentation claim that every owned key buffer is wiped must match all owned scalar temporaries, or state a narrower supported guarantee.
findings.observed: These private-scalar temporaries are created as plain values and leave scope without explicit zeroization.
findings.impact: This limits the secret-lifecycle guarantee. Residual memory exfiltration was not demonstrated; dependency/compiler/register erasure is a separate limitation.
findings.recommendedFix: Use zeroizing owned bindings where practical and revise blanket guarantees to describe unavoidable compiler/dependency copies honestly.
findings.requiredVerification: Review all private scalar conversions and early returns; add meaningful zeroization/lifetime regression evidence without claiming physical erasure of registers.

findings.title: Hidden-wallet count remains in terminal history after the private screen clears
evidence: Source trace of choice::record outside the private-screen lifetime.
findings.reproduction: Trace show_wallet returning after its private screen is cleared, then choice::record(&format!("Wallet {number}"), "24 words, shown and cleared") in wallets::run.
findings.expected: The claim that nothing records how many hidden wallets were used must include the visible terminal transcript, or explicitly exclude it.
findings.observed: Each derived-wallet reveal is followed on the ordinary screen by a numbered Wallet 1, Wallet 2, and so on record. These labels can remain in scrollback or a terminal-session recording.
findings.impact: An observer of the terminal transcript can learn the count of wallets opened in that session. No mnemonic or password is disclosed by this label, and this is outside the formal container/disclosure-only experiment.
findings.recommendedFix: Avoid count-revealing records after the private screen, or narrow the documentation and provide an intentional private-session mode that clears these records.
findings.requiredVerification: Capture an ordinary PTY session using bounded synthetic inputs and confirm no persistent per-wallet count appears when the documented private mode is used.

findings.title: Cosmos and Injective wallet references accept the wrong Bech32 checksum variant
findings.reproduction: Run wallet_bech32_variant.py: re-encode the public Cosmos/Injective vector payloads with Bech32m, then call production Address parsing and find_address.
findings.expected: Cosmos SDK account addresses require Bech32, not Bech32m. Invalid references must be rejected before recovery or identity comparison.
findings.observed: cosmos19rl4cm2hmr8afy4kldpxz3fka4jguq0afua36h and inj1npvwllfr9dqr8erajqqr6s0vxnk2ak55k94rgq are accepted and reported as matching wallet addresses. Generic bech32::decode accepts both checksum variants.
findings.impact: An invalid chain address can be treated as an independent wallet-identity reference. This is a validation/identity-contract defect, not a demonstrated incorrect private-key derivation.
findings.recommendedFix: Require the exact Bech32 variant for Cosmos/Injective while preserving Bech32m for address types that require it.
findings.requiredVerification: Retain literal invalid references and valid public vectors; test Bech32/Bech32m variant mismatch, HRP, casing, payload size, and every other supported Bech32 address family.

findings.title: Rekey warns about dependent wallets but omits the required preservation confirmation
evidence: Source trace against reviewed specification README application requirements.
findings.reproduction: Trace rekey::run from its warning through confirmation and creation of the replacement. Compare the updated specification application requirement.
findings.expected: Before proceeding, every user must explicitly confirm that affected wallets have moved their funds or have independently usable verified backups; the question must not expose which derived wallets exist.
findings.observed: The warning is displayed universally, but no explicit funds-or-backups preservation confirmation is obtained before re-encryption proceeds.
findings.impact: A required guard against loss of dependent-wallet access is absent. The encryption operation itself still round-trips; this finding concerns the supported rekey workflow.
findings.recommendedFix: Add the same explicit preservation confirmation for every user before proceeding; abort safely when it is not confirmed, and retain the statement that old copies are not revoked.
findings.requiredVerification: Test both choices and cancellation through the actual command path; ensure no new container is emitted before confirmation and no question requests hidden-wallet identities/passwords.

findings.title: The seed-check description omits bytes included by the implementation
findings.reproduction: Run seed_check.py with the public TREZOR fixture, counter 76562, and official English wordlist. Compare the documented tag || seed with actual tag || BE32(ENT) || seed.
findings.expected: The draft profile description and current implementation must identify the same byte-level predicate.
findings.observed: The implementation hash is 0000e86481bdfe6dbf45e6e41fba4f309fcf09d3f0af2fe3f46736c663840853, which passes. Omitting ENT produces f2c9f7654eb84903d2a508cdf7ef27f9e4d57fff54b6e13ee35ddabbc9278dbf, which fails.
findings.impact: An independently written recovery program following the prose can disagree about a prepared wallet. This is a draft-profile description mismatch, not a mismatch in suites 3/4 encryption.
findings.recommendedFix: Specify ASCII domain MHFE-WALLET-CHECK-SEED-1 without NUL, BE32 entropy length in bits, raw 64-byte BIP39 seed, canonical English mnemonic, NFKD passphrase, nonempty passphrase, and first 16 digest bits zero. Separate implemented draft behavior from future variants.
findings.requiredVerification: Retain a public no-Argon fixture in the specification and two independent implementations; verify exact bytes, all relevant entropy lengths, Unicode, empty passphrase rejection, and leading-bit semantics.

findings.title: Seed-check security, entropy and decoy claims exceed the stated model
evidence: Source/model comparison; related exact-byte reproduction in seed-check.
findings.reproduction: Read the implemented seed-check description and code module comments. Evaluate the fixed-passphrase rejection-sampling distribution and false-match probability, then distinguish a fixed decoy passphrase from a passphrase that the owner may search.
findings.expected: A 16-bit condition is a probabilistic consistency filter. Under a balanced ideal predicate and fixed BIP39 passphrase, accepted entropy is approximately ENT-16 bits; attack estimates and deniability must be scoped to explicit procedures and distributions.
findings.observed: The text says only the right phrase/passphrase passes, that no protection is lost, that resistance equals the unconditioned profile and that a second passphrase fails. Wrong pairs can pass with probability about 2^-16; deliberately selecting another passphrase can also find a passing result in about 2^16 seed computations. The prior uniform-source deniability theorems do not automatically apply to this conditioned source. The new-wallet help repeats the categorical decoy/passphrase failure and claims that a passing phrase shows MHFE provenance.
findings.impact: These claims can cause users or reviewers to treat a filter as unique wallet identification, a search estimate as an attack lower bound, or an existing theorem as covering a new source distribution. No cheaper complete attack or break of MHFE is established by this audit.
findings.recommendedFix: State conditional entropy (~240 bits for new 24-word creation), false positives and prior dependence; keep the independent strong BIP39 passphrase recommendation; describe the pair-testing procedure without optimality claims, address-comparison savings, and separate decoy strategies. Require a new experiment/proof before extending deniability guarantees.
findings.requiredVerification: Review revised statements against the explicit probability model; preserve warnings that a match is not wallet identity and a failure is meaningful only when this profile was used; verify the creation/check/rekey UI uses those distinctions.

findings.title: The disclosure-simulation corollary does not specify the wallet-record oracle
evidence: Reviewed deniability experiment and corollary source.
findings.reproduction: Compare the prepared-disclosure simulator with the experiment defining wallet-record lookups. Its sampled record must remain consistent with later queries on the sampled wallet.
findings.expected: A simulation statement involving a record oracle must say whether the simulator programs it or uses an already fixed public ledger.
findings.observed: The corollary samples a usage record from the container alone without specifying record-oracle programming or consistency with subsequent lookups.
findings.impact: The broad wording can be read as a claim about a fixed real blockchain that is not justified by the supplied simulator. Theorem 1/2 are not disproved by this clarification request.
findings.recommendedFix: Restrict the corollary to the synthetic fresh-record experiment with explicitly consistent oracle programming, or prove the corresponding statement for the intended fixed-ledger experiment.
findings.requiredVerification: Check the simulator and adversary view step by step, including repeated lookups and the hidden real-wallet record; retain the stated theorem bounds separately.

limitations: This is a full-scope first-party audit with incomplete execution, not a fully executed end-to-end or release acceptance audit.
No full-size Argon2 replay, full-size independent OpenSSL vector replay, canonical Docker rebuild, release archive verification or current remote CI or freshly fetched advisory database check ran.
No actual final-browser CSP, worker cancellation, viewport, mobile or cross-platform Windows/macOS/ARM acceptance ran. WASM compilation is not browser execution.
No cryptographic security proof, exhaustive absence-of-bugs claim or independent expert certification. Reviewed primitives and integration are not a complete upstream audit.
The new wallet seed check is an explicitly marked draft creation profile. Normative core suites 3/4 are unchanged; missing README normative profile definition alone is not a core-conformance defect.
Related specification was dirty at capture. Later owner-authorized Electrum reference follow-up must be identified separately from the reviewed baseline; no production remediation is claimed.

Initial socket test failures were sandbox PermissionDenied results; successful scoped loopback rerun is recorded separately. Initial failed memory probe was a harness/allocation issue, not an extra product finding.
Only public BIP39 fixtures and synthetic passwords were used. No funds, user secrets, transaction broadcasting, commit, push or release operation occurred.
